name: seed_benchmark
description: NEEDS TWO PATH SUBSTITUTIONS BEFORE IT WILL RUN -- see _model_paths below. How much of the agent's win rate is the training seed? Six models, each as the pure-network agent against SakkirinaSolo over 400 games each from one seed_base: the five per-seed models from scripts/slurm_train.sh, plus the shipped model as a sixth point on the same seed_base so it sits in the same distribution rather than beside it.
_first_run_was_invalid: The first run of this config is invalid. Its results are kept under
Job 4457064, 2400 games, all completed cleanly. The five seed rows gave win rates of
Each seed model carried 14,000-19,000 subnormal weights, from training on x86 rather
than on Apple Silicon, which flushes denormals in hardware. Subnormal arithmetic
leaves onnxruntime's fast path, so the seed models ran at a median 640-790 us per
inference against the shipped model's ~58 us, and completed roughly 1,350-1,510
evaluations per turn against the shipped row's 6,401: about a quarter of the search,
in an experiment premised on the six models differing only in training seed.
No game failed, timed out or was disqualified, and the win rates looked like
ordinary seed variance. The only symptom was the evaluations-per-turn column.
The five models were re-exported with denormal flushing (training/export_to_onnx.py
zeroes |w| < 1e-30 by default). They run at 44-50 us, and
tools/compare_onnx_models.py finds zero output difference across 2000 real states
per seed. allowed_onnx_sha256 and the per-matchup notes carry the re-exported
hashes; the old ones must not be re-added.
The shipped row (tasks 2000-2399) has no subnormal weights and ran at 6,401
evaluations per turn. Those results are valid and were kept.
_check_before_interpreting: Before interpreting the rerun, check the evaluations-per-turn column.
Every seed row should land near the shipped row's ~6,400 evaluations per turn. A
seed row at ~1,400 did not run the re-exported model; most likely SOT_MODEL_PATH
still points at a pre-flush .onnx, or a stale copy was left in place. The first run
failed this way with plausible win rates. allowed_onnx_sha256 rejects the old files
and the per-row hash readback (_what_the_pin_guarantees) checks each row's model; the
column is the direct check on search volume.
_model_paths: Every SOT_MODEL_PATH below must be edited before submitting. Two substitutions:
CHANGE_ME_HPCWORK   -> the literal expansion of $HPCWORK on your cluster
CHANGE_ME_REPO_ROOT -> the absolute path of this checkout,
The paths must be absolute. A relative path is resolved against two different
- the game runs with cwd=GameRunner/bin/Release/net8.0, and the bot calls
File.Exists on the same string from there.
A relative path can pass the harness and miss in the bot, which then logs the
rejection and falls back to GameRunner's copy of the shipped model. Every seed row
would then benchmark the shipped model.
$HPCWORK is not expanded: no shell runs between this file and the bot, so a literal
"$HPCWORK/..." is not found. Substitute the expanded path by hand.
An unedited config cannot run: tools/benchmark_cluster.py aborts the task with exit 1
and no result file if SOT_MODEL_PATH does not exist, which CHANGE_ME_* paths fail.
_what_the_pin_guarantees: allowed_onnx_sha256 lists all six hashes and is checked per task against the file
that task's SOT_MODEL_PATH names. That is a set check: it guarantees the task loaded
one of the six known models, not that seed 3's row loaded seed 3's model.
A separate check covers that. After every game the harness reads back the sha256
the bot logged in PregamePrepare and requires it to equal that row's model hash; a
mismatch, or no such line, fails the task and writes no result. Every result JSON
also carries a 'loaded_models' block recording what each bot loaded.
The shipped model's 86e0f9a8... is on the allowed list here because it is one of
the six rows. It is absent from ablation_benchmark.json, where no row should load it
and listing it would let a fallback to GameRunner's built-in copy pass the set check.
To check the files by hand before submitting:
and compare against the table in REPRODUCE.md section 3.
_comparability: The shipped model is a matchup here rather than a number copied in. Its 79.3%
against SakkirinaSolo came from alpha_sweep.json at alpha0=0, with seed_base
20260922; this config uses 20260928, so different deals and a different sample.
Here it runs on the same seed_base as the five seeds.
The rows are still not paired: seed = seed_base + task_id and task ids run
contiguously across matchups, so each matchup plays a different 400 games. They are
six independent samples from one population. Read differences against the Wilson
intervals the aggregator prints, not as a ranking.

matchups.note: The shipped model, on the same seed_base as the five seeds so it is a sixth point in the same distribution -- see _comparability. Its val loss is not in this table on purpose: 0.4034 was measured on a DIFFERENT validation set from the seeds' and is not comparable to theirs. Set explicitly rather than left unset so the plan and every result JSON record which model this row used; leaving it unset would resolve to GameRunner's own copy, which is the same file but says so nowhere. Last in the config, so it can be dropped by simply not submitting its task-id range without renumbering any seed row.
